edited_statements.note: The Absolute Suffers from Remoteness and Abstractness
edited_statements.before: But from the human point of view, no one can pretend that it doesn't suffer from the faults of remoteness and abstractness.
edited_statements.after: But from the human point of view, no one can pretend that the absolutistic brand doesn't suffer from the faults of remoteness and abstractness.
edited_statements.why: The referent of 'it' (the Absolute conception) sits in a sentence not in the notes; the source's own name 'the absolutistic brand' (added as a name span with its own footnote) lets the note stand alone.

hard_calls: 'If the Absolute means this, and means no more than this' refers back to the cash-value statement, so notes 11 holds both and runs to about 210 words.
Note 4 keeps the 'But,' fragment and the 'them' / 'the brand of pantheism offered' references; no source name repairs 'them' short of merging with notes 2-3, which would be too long.
Note 2 keeps 'It is far too intellectualistic' with the idealism statement it refers to.
The 'William James' name span in note 9 was already added at stage 1 and is kept as is.
Note 1 is a single-sentence thesis note; merging it with note 2 was considered but they are separate ideas.
Notes 7 and 8 are split because the pragmatic principle of theological truth (8) is a distinct proposition from pragmatism's open attitude (7).
